title: Secondary School Certificate Class IX Model Examination Paper 2026 and Onwards — Chemistry Paper III (Practical)
objective: To demonstrate the electroplating of copper metal on iron strip using CuSO4 solution.

tasks.prompt: Set the apparatus and perform the experiment. Do not write the method. (Examiner’s observation)
tasks.solution: Student cleans iron strip with sandpaper, connects it to negative terminal (cathode), connects pure copper plate to positive terminal (anode), immerses both in 1.0 M CuSO4 acidified solution, and switches on DC power supply to observe uniform reddish-brown copper deposit.

tasks.prompt: Write ONE precautionary measure that should be taken during the experiment.
tasks.solution: Ensure the iron strip is thoroughly cleaned and polished with sandpaper/dilute acid before electroplating to remove all grease, rust, or oxide film, ensuring uniform adherence.

tasks.prompt: Why is electroplating an important process for industries?
tasks.solution: Electroplating protects base metals from atmospheric corrosion and rusting, improves surface hardness and wear resistance, and enhances aesthetic appearance (shine and decorative value).

Circuit diagram showing battery (DC source), switch, rheostat/ammeter, beaker with CuSO4 electrolyte solution, copper anode (+) connected to positive terminal, and iron strip cathode (-) connected to negative terminal.

tasks.prompt: Write any TWO examples of non-electrolytes.
tasks.solution:
1. Glucose / Sucrose (sugar) aqueous solution.
2. Urea solution / Ethanol (alcohol).

tasks.prompt: Why are metals good conductors of electricity?
tasks.solution: Metals possess delocalised valence electrons that are free to move throughout the metallic lattice under an applied potential difference.

tasks.prompt: Evaluation of student practical laboratory notebook and continuous assessment record.
tasks.solution: 2 Marks awarded for complete, verified, and signed practical journal records.
